turns.content: What brings you in today? Can you describe the main issues or symptoms you are experiencing?

I’ve been having a really hard time following through on my work. I start both class assignments and freelance projects feeling really motivated, but I only seem to actually finish them when there’s some kind of last‑minute crisis or deadline, and it’s starting to mess with my grades and clients.
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse or interrupting others in conversations, or is it more about struggling to focus and complete tasks?

It’s definitely more about struggling to focus and actually complete things. I do catch myself jumping in and cutting people off in group projects or conversations sometimes, but the part that really causes problems is starting projects excited and then stalling out or getting distracted until there’s a deadline panic.
How often do you find it difficult to stay focused on tasks, even when you’re interested in them?

Pretty much every day. Even with stuff I actually like—like a data science lecture or a UX project—I can usually stay really focused for maybe ten minutes, and then my brain drifts off and I either end up rewinding the same part over and over or stalling out halfway through the project unless there’s some urgent deadline.
Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these difficulties with focus and completing tasks?

Honestly, it’s been there since I was a kid—teachers used to write things like “bright but daydreams and rushes,” and I’d forget to turn in homework I’d actually done. It’s gotten a lot worse over the last year and a half, though, since my upper‑division data science classes and freelance work started requiring way more sustained focus and planning.
Do you feel that your impulsivity or difficulty with attention affects your relationships or social interactions significantly?

Yeah, it does affect things. I get distracted really easily in conversations and I’ll fidget or bounce my leg in class or meetings, which people sometimes comment on, and I have a bad habit of interrupting or jumping in before others are finished, which I know can annoy friends or group‑project partners.
Can you describe how your impulsivity or difficulty with attention has impacted your relationships with friends or family?

With friends, I’ll zone out mid‑conversation or get caught up on my phone, and they’ll have to repeat themselves or call me out for not really listening, which has caused a few arguments. I also tend to blurt things out or interrupt when I get excited, so I’ve had people tell me I talk over them, and my family sometimes feels like I’m not fully present when we’re together because I’m restless or mentally somewhere else.
Have you ever noticed that your impulsivity, such as interrupting others or acting on urges, happens more frequently in specific situations or environments?

Yeah, it’s definitely worse in certain situations. In group project meetings or when I’m hanging out with friends and get excited about an idea, I’ll jump in and interrupt more, and when I’m waiting in office hours or in a coffee line I get really antsy and have to fight the urge to cut in or rush things. It’s less of a problem in more structured one‑on‑one situations where I’m really aware I need to wait my turn.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever had any significant issues with organization or managing time effectively?

Yeah, that’s a big problem for me. I constantly underestimate how long things will take, overcommit to projects, and then miss or nearly miss class and client deadlines, and I’ve even had to withdraw from a course and almost lost a freelance client because of it. I also forget routine stuff like replying to important emails or paying my share of bills until there’s a reminder or a late notice.
Can you describe how these difficulties with organization and time management have affected your daily life or responsibilities?

It makes everything feel like it’s on fire all the time. I’m either scrambling to catch up on overdue assignments and client work or dealing with emails and bills I forgot about, so my days end up being a series of mini‑crises instead of anything planned, and it’s really stressful and exhausting.
How do these difficulties with attention and organization affect your overall mood or stress levels?

When I fall behind or realize I’ve missed something, my stress just spikes and I go into panic‑mode marathons to catch up. Afterward I usually feel really drained and discouraged with myself, and the pattern makes me pretty anxious about my grades, my freelance reputation, and whether I’m going to screw up future internships or jobs.
